The green sunfish is a common species of Lepomis. This species is very aggressive and prolific when breeding. This species often is introduced to places where it is not native and out competes native sunfish species. This species is rather reclusive and prefers to spend its days in rock piles or wood piles. They are often confused with warmouth sunfish because of their similar body shape and large gaping mouths. They can be told apart by the body color (green sunfish being a drag green color, with blue jading, purple hue and orange/white edges on the fins) warmouth are brown in color, have much larger jading on the body, have a slightly larger mouths and tend to have red eye. The location is a bit approximate, it was past the Hidden Creek Trail and far before the entrance to the park further on.

Photos 1-12 and 15-16 were edited to have a Custom White Balance in Photoshop (Photoshop's preset).
Photos 4-9, and 13-14 were brightened.
Photos 17-19 weren't edited.
